rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: resolving the mood early steals M3's teaching moment. Strategy doc states M2 mood verbatim: 'grounded competence — "I can feel when a plan is good before approving it, and I know the move is two reads, not one."' The module's Meta block echoes this exact line ('**Mood target:** grounded competence — ...'), and the mood is held open, not resolved: '## Next' (no-M3 branch) ends on 'Come without one and you'll be picking while the walk is already underway. Your call' — forward tension, not closure. Big Idea ('you are the one who can tell the difference') sets up the exercise rather than resolving it.
Rule scopes to modules whose deliberate mood is 'unease'. Strategy doc names M2's mood as 'grounded competence', not unease — this rule's condition doesn't fire on this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: naming the module after a failure mode primes shame instead of a positive discipline. Big Idea reads 'The first plan is plausible. Plausible isn't good enough, and you are the one who can tell the difference' — no failure word (no fabrication/hallucination/violation). Key Concepts bullets use positive framing throughout ('Structure is persuasive', 'A plan with a specific file list has made decisions'), no failure-mode leads. What-You'll-Learn verbs (Run, Push back, Walk down, Spot, Extract) are discipline verbs, not failure nouns.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check (cross-module sequencing honored, no front-running)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: front-running a downstream teaching moment spends it before the room earns it. Strategy doc: 'the skill reveal ... lands in M3 as authoring material' and 'M3 carries the first Skill use + first subagent + first authoring together.' The module's grill-me walk-down is inlined as 'the walk-down-branches prompt' with no mention of skills, Skill authoring, or subagents anywhere in body. '## Next' (earn-the-trust branch) reads 'At M3 you point the same move at a feature you're shipping' — matches strategy doc's M3 framing verbatim ('M3 starts with a feature you're shipping, not a bot you're building'), confirming no drift.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts (>=2-3 theme-instances)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a module that teaches tactics with no theme-instance ships technique without the worldview underneath it. Walked each of the 6 bullets against the strategy doc's 6 named themes (90%-correct / compounding / mirror / self-aware-grain-of-salt / capture-your-world / non-agentic-default): bullet 1 ('Assume about 10% of it is wrong and go find which part') is a direct instance of theme 1 (90% correct), explicitly cross-referenced in the module's own maintainer block as inheriting M1's attested prior. Bullet 6 ('A rule that doesn't load doesn't exist... Fixing the plan is the first loop; changing the rule that shaped it is the second... double-loop learning') is an instance of theme 2 (compounding) and theme 5 (capture-your-world) — the task-shaping-rule artifact is exactly 'capture your world' made concrete per the strategy doc's own description of that exercise. Two clear theme-instances clears the >=2-3 bar (2 counted at ceiling of range, module-specific language, not lectured-before-doing).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs (1-3, no label/bold, variety across adjacent modules)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a labelled/bolded or reused-verbatim breadcrumb reads as trainer-bait or a dead refrain. Bullet 1's breadcrumb clause 'Assume about 10% of it is wrong and go find which part' carries no 'Remember:' label and no bold wrapper (checked raw source line 57). Checked adjacent modules for repeat: getting-going.md (M1) Key Concepts (lines 57-62) carries no 10%-themed or double-loop-themed breadcrumb; earn-the-trust.md (M3) Key Concepts (lines 74-79) carries no repeat of either theme's breadcrumb either — no verbatim or near-verbatim collision within the two-module window. Bullet 6's 'double-loop learning' is an attributed named-model teaching line (Argyris/Schön, matching the module's own §Lecture 'How instructions grow'), not a §6 breadcrumb-shaped clause, so it is exempt from the breadcrumb-form checks (label/bold/length) rather than failing them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: What You'll Learn shape — capability register, theme verbs lead, no apparatus tails
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: syllabus-register or apparatus-laden bullets read as curriculum-describing-itself rather than a peer describing new capability. All 5 bullets (lines 18-22) lead with a concrete verb + immediate object: 'Run plan mode on a real multi-file task and judge the plan against five criteria', 'Push back twice on the plan via *No, keep planning*, surfacing what the agent didn't see', 'Walk down unresolved branches, with a recommended answer per branch', 'Spot approval inflation in a plan whose structure makes it look decided', 'Extract task-shaping rules from two sources, your plan session and one story ticket, into a .md file you place'. Checked all four apparatus failure modes: no Bloom-tag parentheticals; no pedagogical-mechanism tails ('by mapping X to Y'-shaped); no author-defence asides ('not a...' hedges); no didactic taxonomy-stamp colons. 'against five criteria' and 'into a .md file you place' are carve-out (a)/(c) shapes — outcome-artifact naming and a one-line operational anchor, not definition-stamping. None of the 7 recurring strategic-theme verbs (Compound/Earn/Mirror/Ground/Introspect/Sharpen/Capture) fit these five bullets' concrete objects (a plan, branches, a rule) better than the discipline verbs used — no grammar-fit violation to flag.
